rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh pursued Moses with his military force and chiefs, so the punishment engulfed all of them.
rows.anchor: the Pharaoh followed Moses (sws) with all his military might and all his nobles and chiefs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalaf literally means passing and can refer to good or evil predecessors; here Pharaoh’s people became an evil tale of the past, warning Quraysh against their way.
rows.anchor: We destroyed them in such a manner that they became an ancient tale.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathalan means an example or sample; here it is a bad example meant to teach the fate of those arrogant before God.
rows.anchor: We made them such an evil example that people could learn a lesson about the fate of those who show arrogance before God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the same purpose as the earlier accounts of Abraham and Moses, the following verses briefly recount Jesus, who also called people to monotheism.
rows.anchor: For the very purpose the account of Abraham (sws) and Moses (sws) were related earlier

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’s claimed followers adopted religious innovations against his teaching and elevated him to divinity.
rows.anchor: those who claimed to be his followers were afflicted with religious innovations and they fabricated these innovations as blatant defiance of his teachings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh polemicists claim the Qur’an praises Jesus and suggest their angelic deities are superior, misleading followers about the Qur’an’s purpose.
rows.anchor: the quarrelsome elements among the Quraysh work up the mischief that this person praises Jesus (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an presents Jesus as God’s servant and messenger who called people to the same monotheism as the other prophets.
rows.anchor: The fact is that the Qur’ān mentions him as a servant of God and His messenger; he too called people towards the same monotheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities invoked besides God are unaware that people worship and call on them.
rows.anchor: the deities themselves are unaware that they are being worshipped and being called for help.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day, the invoked deities will become the worshippers’ enemies instead of helping them.
rows.anchor: On the Day of Judgement, these deities instead helping them would become their enemies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People overawed by the Qur’an’s reasoning dismiss it as magic and call the Prophet an impostor; Islahi says such obdurate people merit no attention.
rows.anchor: regard it to be magic and regard the Prophet (sws) to be an imposter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told that he is not the first messenger: many came before him with the same traits and characteristics.
rows.anchor: he is not the first messenger of this world; many messengers have preceded him; he has the same traits and characteristics as the previous messengers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those opposing the Prophet under Jewish or Christian influence should contemplate the evil fate they are approaching.
rows.anchor: these people are opposing him, then they should fully contemplate the evil fate they are going to meet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A witness from Israel has testified to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: a great witness of the Israelites has already borne witness to him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s predictions are recorded in the Torah.
rows.anchor: whose predictions are recorded in the Torah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents should not use the fact that poor people believe in the Prophet as an excuse to reject him.
rows.anchor: if poor people are professing faith in him, then they should not make this as an excuse to not embrace faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe acknowledge natural rights and honor their parents; youthful sins do not define them because they repent rather than live sinfully.
rows.anchor: they may have committed sins in their youth while being overwhelmed with emotions; however, they never adopted a sinful life

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At forty, the upright turn sincerely to God, asking gratitude for blessings to themselves and their parents, pleasing deeds, and good descendants.
rows.anchor: When they reached the ripe age of forty, they turned towards God with full sincerity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives these upright people’s sins and includes them among the dwellers of Paradise.
rows.anchor: God will forgive the sins of such upright people and will include them among the dwellers of Paradise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject the message live carelessly, disregard God’s and parents’ rights, and answer parents’ warnings about resurrection with scorn and claims that they are ancient tales.
rows.anchor: they scolded them by saying that this is mere bluff and that they will never profess faith in these nonsensical things

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives each group reward or punishment according to its deeds and wrongs no one.
rows.anchor: God will reward or punish both these types of people in accordance with their deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogant rejecters who used poor believers as an excuse will be told that their share of good things was spent in earthly life and humiliation awaits them in Hell.
rows.anchor: they have taken their share of good things in the previous world; here nothing except ignominy awaits them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of the people of ‘Ād is cited as a warning to Quraysh.
rows.anchor: The example of the people of ‘ Ād is cited to warn the Quraysh who

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the unlettered people’s language was Arabic, mentioning that language refers to the Arabs themselves.
rows.anchor: the language of these unlettered people was Arabic; thus a reference to their language is in fact a reference to the Arabs themselves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One objective of the Qur’an is to warn those unjust to themselves through polytheism and disbelief, allowing reform before consequences arrive.
rows.anchor: people who have been unjust to themselves by being incriminated with polytheism and disbelief be informed of their fate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book’s second objective is an eternal glad tiding for the righteous, expressed as a noun because it is the Book’s real objective.
rows.anchor: allude to the second objective of this Book: it is a great and eternal glad tiding for the righteous.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In contrast to those who wrong themselves, the doers of good are people who guard their abilities and live within their Creator’s limits.
rows.anchor: it refers to people who guarded all their potentials and abilities and spent their lives within the limits stipulated by their Creator.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse elaborates the glad tiding: those who affirmed God alone and steadfastly maintained that declaration will have no fear or sorrow and will dwell in Paradise as reward.
rows.anchor: they will neither have any fear of the future nor any sorrow of the past

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This section further explains the earlier categories: the Qur’an appeals to upright, truth-sensitive people who control emotion and recognize their parents’ rights; indifferent people should be expected to keep their ways and meet their destined fate.
rows.anchor: a further elaboration of the two categories of people referred to earlier by the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains how an upright person naturally develops an understanding of rights and obligations.
rows.anchor: evolution and development of the comprehension of rights and obligations takes place or should take place in an upright and worthy person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness to parents is ingrained in human nature and taught by all God’s prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: He has also ingrained this directive in man’s nature and all the prophets of God and righteous people also taught this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across religions, parents have the greatest right after God; awareness of their right is often the first right a person understands.
rows.anchor: In all religions of the world, this is an acknowledged reality that after God the parents have the greatest right on a person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Understanding parents’ rights leads a person to recognize God and His greater rights.
rows.anchor: It is through the comprehension of his parent’s right that he reaches God and the comprehension of His rights.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rights of God and parents are the two greatest rights, from which other rights branch.
rows.anchor: And these two are the greatest rights on a person and from these two emanate the branches of various other rights.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an infant, a person regards parents as everything; at maturity, he realizes God created them and is the true Lord and Bestower of Favours.
rows.anchor: he becomes aware of the fact that the real Lord and Bestower of Favours is the one who even created his parents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When parents grow old, children should not see them as a burden but remember that their parents cherished and raised them as infants.
rows.anchor: when he reaches his bloom and they reach old age, he should not consider them to be a burden on him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children owe parents obedience, love, and affection; serving them should not feel burdensome, and they should not speak words of repulsion.
rows.anchor: he should always show obedience to them and show love and affection to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about a mother bearing her child points to the sacrifices every mother necessarily makes for her children.
rows.anchor: refer to the sacrifices which every mother necessarily makes for her children.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children can never repay their parents’ favors, given pregnancy, risky delivery, and the effort of nurturing.
rows.anchor: whatever may the children do, they can never repay the favours of their parents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mother carries a child for months, risks her life in delivery, then feeds it with milk for two years and raises it.
rows.anchor: For two whole years, she feeds the child with her milk with great effort and raises and nurtures it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can match the effort a mother makes for her child.
rows.anchor: The implication is that no one can match her effort.
